faq.q1: How long does a website take?

faq.q2: What do I need to get started?
faq.a2: Nothing but an idea. We guide you through the entire process — from conception through content to go-live.
faq.a3: Hosting and domain costs can vary. Our maintenance packages are optional but recommended.
faq.q4: What if I want changes later?
faq.a4: No problem. With a maintenance package, small changes are included. Larger adjustments are billed as individual services.
faq.q5: Can I edit my website myself?
faq.a5: Yes. If needed, we integrate a CMS (e.g., Sanity or Contentful) so you can update text and images yourself.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.notice: Notice: Some individual provider, storage and contract details have not yet been conclusively confirmed. Public provider standards are expressly distinguished from verified settings of our own accounts.

blocks.text: We process personal data to operate the website, handle enquiries, provide demo features expressly used, organise appointments and protect our systems. The relevant processing depends on the features actually used and the data supplied.

Our retention principle is to use data for its purpose and delete it once that purpose ends, unless legal retention duties or other lawful retention grounds apply. External providers and their technical logs have separate rules.

The website is hosted by **Hostinger**. Access may involve an IP address, time, requested URL, browser/device information and security or error logs. This supports delivery, troubleshooting and abuse prevention. The legal basis is Article 6(1)(f) GDPR, our legitimate interest in a secure and functioning website.

Hostinger’s public DPA generally provides for deletion of customer data 30 days after termination, subject to service-specific terms. This is not a general lifetime for active server logs. The specific contracting entity, server region and log/backup arrangements for our account have not yet been conclusively confirmed.
[Hostinger Data Processing Addendum](https://www.hostinger.com/legal/dpa)

The form requires a name, email address and message. Phone number and subject are optional. There is no separate company field; company information may be included voluntarily in the message. We use these details to respond and, where relevant, prepare an engagement. Depending on the enquiry, this relies on Article 6(1)(b) GDPR for pre-contractual steps involving the data subject, or Article 6(1)(f) GDPR for legitimate business correspondence.

Our server sends form messages through **Resend** to contact@mitcodean.com; the visitor’s submitted address is used as the reply address. Our business mailbox is provided by **Hostinger Email**. The application validates input and origin and uses a hidden field to help identify automated submissions. The delivery path does not provide a separate contact database.

Resend publishes 30-day email-content/log retention for Free/Pro/Scale, seven-day backups and deletion of remaining customer data within 90 days of account termination. Enterprise terms may differ. It states that storage is in the United States; selecting an EU sending region does not change this. Our actual plan and tracking/webhook settings remain to be confirmed.
Enquiry and mailbox data are deleted when their purpose ends under our retention principle. Specific mailbox, archive, forwarding and backup arrangements have not yet been fully documented.
[Resend privacy information](https://resend.com/security/gdpr) · [Resend DPA](https://resend.com/legal/dpa)

The demo processes the currently entered text, selected model and language. Our server sends the text and necessary analysis instructions to the **OpenAI API**. The available models are gpt-4.1-nano and gpt-5-nano. Results are held in the open demo’s state. Drawings and attachments are not uploaded or analysed; the displayed manual approval is a simulation.
Do not enter confidential information, third-party personal data or special categories of personal data. AI results may be incorrect or incomplete and require human review before business use.

The application uses `store=false`. OpenAI’s public documentation states that API data is generally not used for model training without opt-in, and abuse-monitoring logs may normally be retained for up to 30 days, subject to documented exceptions such as legal or necessary protection grounds. `store=false` does not mean no storage.

Our specific contracting/project assignment, data-sharing and retention settings, API region and transfer arrangements remain to be confirmed. The voluntary demo illustrates our services; the final document-specific assignment of its data protection basis remains open.
[OpenAI API data controls](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data)

Protected demo calls are limited to five attempts within a rolling 24-hour window per visitor and network identifier. A minimum interval and global/concurrent-use limits also apply. These protect availability and API budget; the basis is the legitimate interest in preventing abuse under Article 6(1)(f) GDPR.

Processing includes a signed visitor identifier, HMAC-pseudonymised visitor/network identifiers, attempt timestamps and technical reservations. This is not complete anonymisation; several users sharing a network connection may share a limit. The limiter does not store raw enquiry text.

The application supports local file storage and **Upstash Redis**; its code requires shared Redis storage and a verified IP-header configuration for public operation. Whether and in which region Upstash is used in production has not yet been conclusively confirmed.

The counting window is 24 hours. The roughly 24-hour Redis TTL is refreshed on writes and does not guarantee deletion of every record, log or backup after exactly 24 hours. Actual provider/backup periods remain to be confirmed.
[Upstash data processing terms](https://upstash.com/trust/dpa.pdf)

Our [booking link](https://calendly.com/mitco-deansilviu/30min) opens **Calendly** in a new tab. No Calendly widget is embedded in the reviewed website code. When you visit the external page, Calendly processes information supplied there; Diovis uses the booking details it receives to organise the appointment.

Calendly describes US data centres and standard contractual clauses in its DPA as a transfer mechanism. Active booking fields, calendar/meeting connections, account terms and actual retention remain to be confirmed. The legal basis depends on the booking purpose, particularly pre-contractual steps or the legitimate interest in business communication. You can alternatively contact us directly by email or phone.

[Calendly storage and transfers](https://calendly.com/help/data-storage-and-international-data-transfers) · [Calendly deletion functions](https://calendly.com/help/how-to-delete-personal-data-in-calendly)

The application uses cookie/language preferences and demo security identifiers. Consent may not be necessary for strictly necessary terminal access under section 165(3) Austrian TKG 2021; non-essential cookies or embedded services may require prior consent.

Personal data is processed for its purpose and deleted when that purpose ends, unless legal retention duties or other lawful grounds, such as establishing or defending legal claims, apply. This principle covers our own enquiry, correspondence and appointment data.

Provider logs, backups and archives have separate terms. The provider standards above are not blanket Diovis retention periods. Account-specific log, mailbox, archive, backup and deletion procedures have not yet been fully documented. Cookie expiry or a counting window does not automatically delete all related data.

sections.title: Section 1 – Scope and order of precedence

items: These T&C apply exclusively to **business customers (B2B)** in respect of IT, software, automation, network and maintenance services and supplementary website and agency services provided by Diovis. Consumer contracts are not covered by this version.
The specific services, fees and dates are defined by the relevant written offer, statement of work and project or maintenance agreement. **Individually agreed terms take precedence over these T&C.**

The customer's deviating terms apply only if expressly agreed. These T&C must be brought to the customer's attention **before the agreement is concluded** and expressly incorporated into that agreement.

sections.title: Section 2 – Offers and conclusion of agreements

items: A specific offer describes the scope, deliverables, exclusions, fee, payment schedule, term or deadlines and cooperation obligations. Whether it is binding and how long it remains valid are stated in the offer.
An engagement is formed by documented acceptance of an offer or a separate agreement.

Cost estimates must be clearly labelled. There is no automatic agreement to charge for exceeding package prices. Additional services and costs are approved through a documented **change request** before work starts.

sections.title: Section 3 – Scope of services and customer cooperation

items: Only the services individually agreed are owed. They may include business process automation, custom web and desktop applications, interfaces, AI integrations, data preparation and IT infrastructure work. Other services must be stated in the relevant engagement.
Services not expressly included (such as ongoing licence fees, hosting, maintenance, new features or external specialist works) are not automatically included in the project fee.

The customer provides agreed information, contact persons, access and approvals on time and is responsible for the factual correctness of materials and the authority to provide the relevant data and content.
Credentials must be exchanged only through agreed secure channels. Required permissions are returned, restricted or revoked at the end of the engagement as agreed.

sections.title: Section 4 – Third-party providers, cloud services and specialist works

items: As a general rule, the customer orders and pays for **hosting, domains, OpenAI/Anthropic API accounts, cloud software and other recurring third-party services in its own accounts**, unless otherwise agreed for an individual project.
Third-party availability, pricing, terms and intellectual property are governed by their respective providers. Diovis does not give a general guarantee that such services will remain unchanged.

Electrical or cabling works requiring a separate trade authorisation are **not performed by Diovis itself**. If needed, an appropriately authorised specialist company may be engaged by prior arrangement; the contractual relationship, appointment and cost allocation will be established in advance.
Where personal data are processed, sub-processors will be engaged only in compliance with any required data processing agreement.
Fees are determined by the offer. Diovis typically offers packages or fixed fees for clearly defined projects and, where agreed, hourly rates for additional work and support.

Where expressly agreed in the engagement, the standard payment schedule is **50% upon order acceptance and 50% after go-live**. For larger projects, a **50% / 30% / 20%** milestone schedule may be individually agreed. The corresponding milestones and payment triggers are defined in the specific engagement; that individual agreement prevails.
Unless otherwise stated in the offer, the payment term is **14 days from the invoice date**.

Diovis currently applies the Austrian small business VAT exemption. Supplies covered by that exemption are invoiced **without Austrian VAT being charged** (section 6(1)(27) Austrian VAT Act). Cross-border supplies and any change in VAT status are invoiced in accordance with the applicable tax law.
Chargeable additional services and changes must be documented and approved before implementation.
Binding deadlines and milestones must be expressly stated in the engagement. Delays caused by insufficient or late customer cooperation may require a documented change of schedule.

Changes to the agreed scope, technical prerequisites or acceptance criteria require a separate agreement (change request). Any price and schedule implications must be communicated before implementation.

For work capable of acceptance, deliverables and acceptance criteria are defined in the engagement. The customer is given the opportunity to check the agreed criteria, and the results are documented in an acceptance record.
Go-live and acceptance can be separate events. Fee milestones are governed by the relevant agreement.
Deviations are documented and handled in accordance with the applicable legal and contractual obligations.
The agreed project package includes an **accompanied introduction period of 14 calendar days from the agreed go-live date**, covering the functions agreed in the project and their use.

This covers questions concerning the **use and agreed functions** and reasonable assistance with initial use. No fixed number of questions or training hours is promised or capped; the service remains limited to the purpose of introducing the agreed deliverable.

New functionality, additional integrations, materially new requirements or separate further development are not included and require a new engagement. Mandatory statutory defect rights remain unaffected.

The introduction does not establish uninterrupted availability or a response commitment independent of a separate SLA. Specific support windows, response commitments, rates and any night emergency service are defined exclusively in the separate customer agreement.

sections.title: Section 9 – Copyright, software licence and source code

items: Unless otherwise agreed, Diovis retains its rights in its own pre-existing and reusable components and any source code not expressly supplied. Third-party rights and open-source licences remain unaffected.

After full payment, the customer is generally granted a **non-exclusive, perpetual right to use the delivered software for the expressly agreed business purpose**. Territorial, functional and organisational scope must be specified in the project agreement where necessary.

**Source code delivery**, exclusive exploitation rights, separately negotiated modification rights and resale rights are **not automatically included**. Such rights can be expressly agreed for an additional fee.
Mandatory rights of lawful software users remain unaffected; in particular, statutory use and interoperability rights are not excluded wholesale.
Customer names, logos, project details or results may be used as references **only after the customer's prior express approval**.

**Ongoing maintenance, on-call services, monitoring and response guarantees arise only under a separately and expressly agreed maintenance/support contract with a service level agreement (SLA).** Completion of a software project alone does not provide any right to a 24/7 emergency service.

Service windows, reporting channels, incident classes, response commitments, absence cover and hourly rates (including an optional critical night service) are defined in the particular maintenance agreement.
An agreed response time concerns only the **first qualified response**, not a guarantee that the issue will be resolved in the same period.

sections.title: Section 11 – Security, AI services and confidentiality

items: Each party treats confidential project information and credentials confidentially according to their sensitivity. Disclosure to authorised staff or service providers is limited to what is necessary and lawful.

For AI integrations, permitted data types, providers, human review requirements, technical limitations and responsibilities are defined in the engagement. AI-generated content is not inherently error-free; agreed performance obligations and review duties depend on the specific contract.

Any security measures actually promised are documented, where appropriate, in a technical and organisational measures (TOM) annex. Unverified measures do not become implemented merely because these T&C mention them.

Each party complies with the data protection rules applicable to its role. If Diovis processes personal data **on behalf of** the customer, an appropriate **Article 28 GDPR data processing agreement**, with suitable TOMs and sub-processor arrangements, must be in place before processing begins.

The **website privacy policy** describes processing in connection with visiting Diovis online services; it does not replace a project-specific data processing agreement or privacy arrangements for customer systems.

Rights and obligations relating to defects are governed by applicable law and valid individual agreements. Specific characteristics, testing procedures and any service levels are defined in the engagement.
Liability is governed by applicable law and any **legally reviewed and effectively agreed** restrictions.
Late payment is governed by the applicable law, including statutory interest and recoverable debt collection costs in business transactions.
Any suspension of further services is permitted only where lawful and validly agreed.

One-off projects are completed according to the specific delivery and acceptance model. The duration, notice periods and consequences of terminating ongoing maintenance are set out in the relevant maintenance contract.
Handover, data return, revocation of access rights, documentation and ongoing software use rights are governed by the specific engagement and any required data processing agreement.

sections.title: Section 16 – Governing law, jurisdiction and languages

items: Austrian law is intended to apply to B2B contracts insofar as effectively agreed and not contrary to mandatory law.
Statutory jurisdiction rules apply.

These T&C are available in German and English. **In the event of inconsistencies, the German version is intended to prevail**, provided that this rule has been validly incorporated into the individual agreement and does not conflict with mandatory law.

about.title: Understand technology. Simplify workflows.
about.description: Diovis is a young, owner-run business for software development, process automation and IT. The person behind it is me: Dean-Silviu Mitco.
about.role: Founder of Diovis · Software development & IT
bio: I completed my IT education at HTL Steyr. Since July 2025, I have been gaining professional software development experience. This technical background informs my work at Diovis.

With Diovis, I want to support businesses where recurring work and technical questions make daily operations more complicated. I start with the requirements and assess which solution is appropriate and feasible.

I live in Losenstein, Upper Austria. Diovis focuses regionally on businesses in Steyr, Steyr-Land and the surrounding area. This is where I want to personally support businesses with their digital workflows and technical requirements.

principles.title: Direct communication
principles.text: You speak with the person working on your requirements and technical implementation.

principles.title: Appropriate solutions
principles.text: Technology follows the need. Possibilities, limitations and open questions are discussed in plain language.

principles.title: Clear next steps
principles.text: Scope and next steps are agreed together. Review and handover are part of implementation.

steps.title: Understand the workflow
steps.text: We discuss the starting point, existing systems and the steps you want to change.

steps.title: Narrow down the options
steps.text: We clarify requirements, priorities and sensible boundaries for a technical solution.

steps.title: Agree on implementation
steps.text: Scope and next steps are agreed on this basis, followed by development, review and handover.
